title: Colonial Bengal: From Plassey to Permanent Settlement
tagline: Company conquest, revenue extraction, famine, and early colonial politics
intro: Follow Bengal from Plassey and Buxar to Diwani rights, famine, Permanent Settlement, and early representative politics.
description: Follow Bengal from late Nawabi rule through Company conquest, revenue experiments, famine pressures, Permanent Settlement, and the politics that reshaped rural society.
seoTitle: Colonial Bengal: Plassey, Buxar, Diwani, Famine and Permanent Settlement
seoDescription: Study colonial Bengal through Plassey, Buxar, East India Company Diwani rights, the 1770 famine, Permanent Settlement, key figures, and sources.
beginnerSummary: Start with Plassey and Buxar to understand how military defeat, fiscal power, and land revenue transformed Bengal.
advancedSummary: Compare battle narratives with revenue institutions, famine vulnerability, zamindari change, and early colonial political representation.

faq.question: Why connect Plassey to Permanent Settlement?
faq.answer: Together they show a shift from military-political takeover to fiscal and landholding structures that shaped colonial rural Bengal.

faq.question: Is this only a military history topic?
faq.answer: No. Battles matter, but the hub emphasizes revenue, famine, land rights, and social consequences after Company rule expanded.

faq.question: Which figures should I compare?
faq.answer: Compare Siraj ud-Daulah, Robert Clive, Mir Jafar, Mir Qasim, Shah Alam II, Warren Hastings, and Cornwallis across conquest and revenue change.

learningPath.reason: Place the topic in period context.
